top_categories.workout_context: 6,800ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
At mile 60 of 93, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
73ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Utah's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
Gran Fondo Utah's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 93 miles.
At Gran Fondo Utah, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 93 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Utah. Train it until it feels boring.
6,800ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Gran Fondo Utah, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
The aerobic base that lets you ride mixed terrain at tempo for 93 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on mixed terrain. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.

race_overlay.heat: June in Payson Memorial Park, 300 S Main St, Payson, UT 84651, USA can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Utah. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Utah’s 93 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Gran Fondo Utah with 6,800ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Gran Fondo Utah requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Durability, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 93 miles of mixed terrain in Payson Memorial Park, 300 S Main St, Payson, UT 84651, USA.
